templates.source: Y8 Summer B1 Angles in parallel lines and polygons · S2 Angles in parallel lines
templates.text: The two lines are parallel. Explain why $z = [[180 - p]]°$.
templates.answer: Co-interior angles between parallel lines add up to 180°, so $z = 180 - [[p]] = [[180 - p]]°$

templates.answer: $b = [[p]]°$ (alternate angles); $c = [[180 - p]]°$ (angles on a straight line)

templates.answer: [[p + q]]° (alternate angles on each side of the parallel line added together)

templates.subtopic: Interior angles of a regular polygon
templates.source: Y8 Summer B1 Angles in parallel lines and polygons · S10 Interior angles of a regular polygon
templates.text: Do regular [[n]]-sided polygons fit together around a point with no gaps? Explain using interior angles.
templates.answer: Interior angle [[(n - 2) * 180 / n]]°; [[360 % ((n - 2) * 180 / n) == 0|if:360 divided by the angle is a whole number, so they do fit/360 divided by the angle is not a whole number, so they do not fit]]

templates.source: Y8 Summer B1 Angles in parallel lines and polygons · S11 Prove simple geometric facts (E)
templates.text: $AB$ and $CD$ are parallel. Angle $a$ = [[p]]°. Work out angle $b$ (alternate to $a$) and angle $c$ (on a straight line with $b$), giving a reason for each step.
templates.answer: $b = [[p]]°$ (alternate angles are equal); $c = [[180 - p]]°$ (angles on a straight line add up to 180°)

templates.source: Y8 Summer B1 Angles in parallel lines and polygons · S11 Prove simple geometric facts (E)
templates.text: Prove that the opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal. In parallelogram $ABCD$, angle $A$ is [[p]]°. Show that angle $C$ is also [[p]]°.
templates.answer: Angle $B$ = 180 − [[p]] = [[180 - p]]° (co-interior angles); angle $C$ = 180 − [[180 - p]] = [[p]]° (co-interior angles)

templates.source: Y8 Summer B1 Angles in parallel lines and polygons · S11 Prove simple geometric facts (E)
templates.text: A triangle has angles [[a]]° and [[b]]° inside it. Prove that its exterior angle at the third vertex is [[a + b]]°.
templates.answer: The third angle is 180 − [[a]] − [[b]] = [[180 - a - b]]° (angles in a triangle). The exterior angle is 180 − [[180 - a - b]] = [[a + b]]° (angles on a straight line)

templates.source: Y8 Summer B1 Angles in parallel lines and polygons · S11 Prove simple geometric facts (E)
templates.text: Prove that the interior angles of a [[n]]-sided polygon add up to [[(n - 2) * 180]]°. (3 marks)
templates.answer: Split the polygon into [[n - 2]] triangles from one vertex. Each triangle has angles adding to 180°, so the total is [[n - 2]] × 180 = [[(n - 2) * 180]]°
